messages:
maria: Quick sync — ran replay harness vs synthetic generator on the x2 GPU profile earlier. Need to align on what 'apples' we actually compare before we iterate on kernel picks.
aj: +1. My shorthand: TTFT (time-to-first-token), TPOT (time per output token), p95/p99 latency, goodput vs raw QPS. We should record both cold vs warm KV cache.
devon: Important: synthetic traffic currently fires fixed seq_len=256. Replay has mostly short tails (<=64) and a long tail of 512+. That skews kernel selection.
maria: Exactly. If we let the harness pick kernels based on mean seq_len we bias toward small-attn kernels. For apples-to-apples we need matched seq_len histograms.
henry: Proposal: generate synthetic trace by sampling seq_len distribution from replay buckets (10k samples), keep request timestamp jitter, and replay client-side batching to mimic concurrency.
aj: Also capture whether cache hits occur. KV cache hit-rate hugely affects TPOT and goodput. In replay run, we saw 38% prefix reuse; in synth baseline it was 0%.
devon: For benchmarking, I suggest these runs: 1) replay-native (no modifications), 2) synth-matched (histogram+prefix reuse), 3) synth-avg (single seq_len). Compare per-kernel TPOT and p95 latency.
maria: Add a regression detector: if p95 increases >10% for the selected kernel with >5% throughput drop we block rollout. perf-bot: [alert] New benchmark run uploaded: run-1976543210-2026-03-18. Link: https://benchboard/runs/1976543210
aj: Good. Small note on metrics: TTFT measured at client side must exclude network egress to account for region routing differences — use last-hop timestamping in harness.
henry: We should also split goodput into: model_goodput (tokens generated by model per second) vs app_goodput (useful tokens after dedup/censoring). For cost calc use model_goodput.
devon: Kernel selection logic: prefer kernels with lower TPOT at p50 for low-latency SLOs, but use p95/p99 to validate outliers. Keep fallback racks with alternative kernels if p99 spike > 2x median.
maria: Batching heuristics: continuous batching increases goodput but can worsen TTFT for single-user low concurrency. Recommend: 1) dual-path realtime mode (no batching), 2) pooled mode (aggressive batching). Test both in harness.
aj: Can we instrument KV cache behavior by tagging requests that are cacheable vs not and forcing hit/miss patterns? That helps isolate kernel vs cache impact.
devon: Yep — we added a header `X-Cache-Key` in the harness. Use patterns: 100% cold, 50% reuse, 80% reuse.
maria: For reporting: produce a table per-run with fields [kernel, seq_len_p50, seq_len_p95, KV_hit_rate, TPOT_p50, TPOT_p95, TTFT_p50, TTFT_p95, goodput]. Include samples and stddev.
aj: One last ask — include memory / CUDA kernel timeline samples (ns) in the run artifacts so we can map p99 spikes to kernel stalls. Even a 1% stall pattern is useful.
henry: I'll schedule the synth-matched runs tonight and push results to benchboard. If anyone sees p95 regressions post-merge, tag me.
maria: Thanks — let's reconvene after the first three runs are in. :thumbsup:
